subject: science
skillName: Fair Tests to Improve a Design
intro: To improve a design, engineers test their model, or prototype, with a fair test. In a fair test you change only one variable at a time and keep everything else the same, so you know what caused any difference. Engineers also look for failure points, the places where the design does not work well, because those show what to improve. After testing, they use the results to make the design better and often test again. Testing one change at a time and studying where a design fails leads to steady improvement.

items.prompt: A team tests two paper airplanes to see which folds fly farther. To be fair, they want to test only the fold. What should they keep the same?

steps: A fair test changes only one variable, here the fold, and keeps everything else the same.
They should use the same paper, the same throwing force, and the same spot to throw from.
Keeping these the same makes sure any difference in distance comes from the fold, not something else.
solution.answer: Keep the paper, throwing force, and starting spot the same, so only the fold is different.

items.prompt: Why does a fair test change only one variable at a time?

steps: If you change more than one thing, you cannot tell which change caused the result.
Changing only one variable means any difference in the result comes from that one change.
This makes the test fair and the results trustworthy.
solution.answer: So you can tell which change caused the result; if more than one thing changes, you cannot be sure what made the difference.

items.prompt: During testing, a toy bridge always cracks at the middle. What is this telling the engineers, and what should they do?

steps: The spot that always breaks is a failure point.
A failure point shows where the design is weakest and needs improvement.
The engineers should strengthen the middle of the bridge and test it again.
solution.answer: The middle is a failure point, so they should strengthen the middle and test the bridge again.

items.prompt: What is a failure point in a design?

steps: A failure point is a place where the design does not work well or breaks.
Finding failure points shows engineers what to improve.
solution.answer: A place where the design does not work well or fails, which shows what to improve.

items.prompt: A student tests a boat's floating by changing the shape AND the material at the same time, then sees it floats better. Why can the student not tell what caused the improvement?

steps: Two variables were changed at once: the shape and the material.
The better floating could be from the new shape, the new material, or both.
Because more than one variable changed, the test is not fair and the cause is unknown.
solution.answer: Because two variables changed at once, so the student cannot tell whether the shape, the material, or both caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A team's parachute falls too fast. Plan a fair test to find out if a larger canopy helps, then explain how the results guide improvement.

steps: Change only the canopy size and keep the string length, weight, and drop height the same.
Drop both parachutes and measure the fall time to compare fairly.
If the larger canopy falls more slowly, the results show that increasing canopy size improves the design, so they make it larger.
solution.answer: Test a larger canopy while keeping everything else the same; if it falls slower, the results show that a larger canopy improves the design.
